key_insight: Simulated quantum layers can improve vision-language accuracy or reduce trainable parameters, but gains depend strongly on placement.
engineering_relevance: Hybrid VLM design should prioritize layer placement and measure computational cost directly, since fewer trainable parameters do not reliably reduce training time or compute.
method: Use LLaVA-OneVision with classically simulated 4- and 8-qubit circuits.
Test basic-ring and strongly entangling circuits at four insertion and four replacement locations.
Compare accuracy and computational cost, and evaluate robustness under six attack settings.
evidence_signal: On Visual Spatial Reasoning, post-projector insertion reaches 80.7% development accuracy (+2.28 percentage points over classical full fine-tuning), while final decoder feed-forward replacement retains 79.22% with 13.07 million fewer trainable parameters.
watch_item: Results rely on classical quantum simulation; real-hardware benefits, broader generalization, and security advantages remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?
